chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Malik Al-Hadrami, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Three things from which no prophet and none below him is safe: reflection on whispers (tafakkur) in the creation, superstition (al-tyarah), and envy (al-hasad); except that the believer does not put his envy into practice.
ai.seo_question: What are the three spiritual trials that even prophets face, and how does a believer differ in handling envy?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies overthinking creation's origins, superstition (al-tiyarah), and envy as universal spiritual trials affecting even prophets, yet distinguishes the believer by their restraint from acting upon envy. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'amal al-hal' (practical application) over mere internal feeling, aligning with the concept that faith is validated through conduct. The warning against tiyarah also connects to the rejection of pre-Islamic Jahiliyyah customs, reinforcing the purification of the heart from subtle shirk-like dependencies.
